200.answer: Q: What is a Modem? A: device that allows you to connect to the Internet. Q: What is a Power cord? A: small black cord with a round end which plugs into a power outlet and provides power to the modem. Q: What is a Fibre port? A: hidden port on the back of the modem where the fibre cable (white or black) is plugged in. It provides an Internet connection to the modem. Q: What are LAN ports? A: yellow ports on the back of the modem which allow you to directly connect your devices to the Internet. Q: How does this affect my services? A: If any cables are unplugged accidentally, your services may be temporarily unavailable.Q: What are we doing in these steps? A: We’re checking to see if your modem and cables are properly connected in order to eliminate this as the possible cause of the problem. Q: What if these instructions don't match my setup? A: Just confirm whether the lights on your modem are all solid white. Q: How do I perform Step 1? A: Locate your modem. Q: How do I perform Step 2? A: Ensure that one end of the power cable is connected to your modem and the other end is plugged directly into a wall outlet. Q: How do I perform Step 3? A: Check if there’s a fibre cable connected to the port labelled “Fibre” on the back of your modem. Do not remove the cable. Q: How do I perform Step 4? A: If you’re using a wired connection, ensure that one end of the Ethernet cable is plugged into the yellow port labelled “LAN” and the other end is connected to your device.
